page: Microsoft Azure E4_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. Its compute resources consist of 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores utilizing two threads per core. The processor architecture provides 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES-NI.

The virtual machine features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB allocation per vCPU. It does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs, necessitating the use of remote persistent storage volumes. In synthetic CPU benchmarks, the system produces moderate single-core results, scoring 1617.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and 1897.98 in stress-ng. Multi-core performance is constrained by the 2-core physical limit, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 3461.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5952.68. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths measure 28.02 GB/sec and 24.29 GB/sec, respectively.

From an architectural standpoint, the E4_v5 provides resource efficiency for memory-centric configurations that do not require high parallel compute density. Operational tests demonstrate 4.41 million operations per second for Redis SET commands and 6.21 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. The primary operational tradeoff involves limited parallel processing headroom under heavy multi-threaded loads and the lack of local ephemeral disks. The instance is appropriate for intermediate in-memory databases, key-value stores, enterprise application backends, and lightweight data transformation workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E4_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 32.0 GB of memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU density. It includes no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, depending entirely on external volumes for disk storage. Benchmark profiles show average single-threaded capability, registering a 1617.0 Geekbench single-core score, alongside modest multi-core capacity with a 3461.0 Geekbench score and a 5952.68 PassMark CPU score. Uncached memory throughput reaches 28.02 GB/sec for reads and 24.29 GB/sec for writes. The instance trades multi-core parallelism for high memory capacity per core, rendering it practical for memory-bound tasks including Redis caching layers, relational databases, business enterprise services, and small to mid-scale data processing.
